data.claim: Three layers, each honest about its limit: (A) a logical correction event replaces fields in derived state but leaves the old text in the log; (B) an operator-gated physical scrub rewrites shard lines and blobs in the working tree, keeping event ids and order, but git history keeps the old text until the operator rewrites it; (C) a leak guard (scan plus write-time redaction from one pattern set and a local forbidden-term list) stops recurrence. Rotation of a leaked secret is the only real remedy.
data.falsifier: A leaked value that survives a scrub in any committed file, blob, derived cache or export; a scrub that changes event ids, order or the folded state of other records; a correction that leaves the old text in a view, brief, search or export; an agent that can run a scrub or have one auto-approved.
data.mechanism: Existing: write-time redaction (core/redact: engine, profiles, secret_shapes; config [log].redact_builtin_shapes, [session].redact_patterns/redact_extra, names from [upstream].redact_extra) covers new writes only; per-kind <kind>.updated events (core/record_fields.py, core/handlers/record_update.py) carry only the NEW field values, so the old text stays in the .recorded event; event id is a digest of the event body (Event.compute_id), so any hand edit of a line is a content_mismatch that doctor --accept-history (services/repairs/accepted.py, which already names 'a secret scrub') lets a person accept; shard-marks (services/shardmarks.py) keep a local count and last event id per shard and report a shrunk shard as lost, accepted by doctor --accept-lost-events; blobs under .ddflow/blobs are named by the sha256 of their canonical body and the event stub pins it, so replacing a blob breaks the address unless the stub is rewritten too; approvals tiers T1/T2/T3 in services/approvals/sites.py, standing policy rules are code-registered per T2 verb (services/approvals/policy.py), so a new T3 verb is outside every policy rule and the retry-threshold rule (RETRY_VERBS lists only four T2 verbs). Best practice: rotate first; history rewrite with git-filter-repo then force push of branches and tags, notify clones and forks, ask the host to purge cached views; event-sourcing erasure uses forgettable payloads (sensitive text held in a separate removable store, event keeps a reference) and crypto-shredding; a tombstone flag alone does not remove data.
data.question: How can a recorded value (a leaked secret, a hostname, a person or organisation name, a wrong fact, a typo) be corrected or removed from an append-only, git-committed event log, and what can honestly be promised?

data.alternatives: Crypto-shredding every payload (rejected: key management for a plain-text git log, large change); forgettable payloads for all free text (rejected: breaks the single-source log, many reads); tombstone flag only (rejected: does not remove data); ddflow rewriting git history (rejected: the operator's call, destructive).
data.consequences: Old text stays in the log after A and in git history after B until the operator rewrites history; the docs and every command output say so. More event kinds and a T3 verb to maintain.
data.context: Records could not be edited after the fact; a superseding record leaves the old text in the log. Leaks (a secret, a hostname, a name) recur.
data.decision: A: a record.corrected event (one kind, strict fold, fields validated against core/record_fields.py) replaces fields of any record kind in derived state and carries who, when, why, field names and digests of old and new values, never the old value. B: ddflow scrub (dry-run by default, person-only) rewrites the working-tree event lines and blobs that hold a literal, replaces it with [scrubbed:<id>], keeps event ids and order, appends a scrub.recorded tombstone (event id, digest after scrub, pattern digest, reason), and tells doctor 'scrubbed' not 'lost' or 'content mismatch'. C: ddflow scan-records searches events, blobs, views and exports for the built-in secret shapes plus a local forbidden-term list and feeds A and B; write-time redaction reads the same pattern set and terms. ddflow never rewrites git history and never pushes.
data.title: Record correction is three layers: logical correction, physical scrub, leak guard

data.alternatives: T2 with policy exclusion (rejected: one config edit from auto-approval); no gate (rejected).
data.consequences: Scrubs always wait for a person; the one-use, one-hour approval conventions apply.
data.context: A scrub rewrites committed history files and is irreversible; a standing window must never decide it.
data.decision: ddflow scrub is a new T3 verb (scrub.apply) at the strongest level, with a new Site row. No [approvals].policy rule and not the retry-threshold rule may cover it (the latter lists only T2 verbs; a test pins that no registered rule or retry verb names a T3 verb or scrub.apply), and typed-chat approval is refused for it even when accept_chat_for_t3 is on. An agent may request a scrub (it files the ask with the dry-run report digest) and may run the dry run; only a person approves. The approval digest binds the literal's digest, the file list and the working-tree state.
data.title: A physical scrub is a person-only T3 act, never auto-approved

data.alternatives: Operator only (slow, the issue repeats); anyone (forgery of history).
data.consequences: Agents can fix their own typos and leaks without waiting; cross-author edits stay gated.
data.context: Agents file most records; the operator owns decisions and rules.
data.decision: An agent may correct a record it authored (same agent id) or any record on an item it holds the lease on, with a required reason; a correction of another agent's or the operator's record needs the person (T2 ask, answered once). A person may correct anything. A correction naming a secret takes the new text through write-time redaction and the audit entry stores only digests (SHA-256, truncated, never of a value shorter than a configured minimum, so a short value cannot be recovered by guessing).
data.title: Who may correct a record

data.body: Level A of D-record-correction-layers (research R-record-correction-2026-11-11). Add a record.corrected event: subject = the record id; data = kind, fields (new values, validated against the record_fields catalogue exactly as <kind>.updated, strict), reason (required, redacted), by, and per field an audit entry holding the field name, a truncated SHA-256 of the old and of the new value (never the old value, never a digest of a value shorter than [records].correct_min_digest_chars), and the correction count. The fold sets the fields and appends the audit entry to the record; show and history list corrections; briefs, search and views read the corrected state. The event is a registered kind (event kinds registry, redaction text field reason, snapshot fixture, compaction-protected). Old text remains in the log; the audit entry and help say so. Knobs: [records].correct_digest_chars (default 12), correct_min_digest_chars, correct_reason_max_chars, correct_max_fields; all layered. Acceptance: tests that fail before: a corrected bug/lesson/research/decision/memory/task/phase/rule shows the new text in state, show and history; a field outside the catalogue fails the strict fold; the audit entry never contains the old value (a planted secret is searched for in the entry and the event line); replay of the log reproduces the corrected state; an older reader skips the kind with a note. Estimated size: M (about 350 lines).
data.title: Logical correction: a record.corrected event, strict fold and audit entry for every record kind

data.body: ddflow correct <id> --field body --text/--from-file --reason ... (or ddflow update --correct) and the same as an action of an existing family tool over MCP (no new top-level tool; tools/list budget), CLI and MCP parity from one declaration, README row, help topic, knob and upgrade-fragment conventions. Permission model per D-correction-permissions: an agent corrects its own records or records of an item it holds; others need a person (T2 ask with --approval re-run); a person corrects anything; every refusal names the nearest verb. The new text passes write-time redaction. Output states that the old text is still in the log and names the scrub and rotate follow-ups. Acceptance: tests that fail before: parity test; agent correcting another agent's record is refused with an ask; own record accepted; reason missing refused; redaction applied to the new text; help and README parity tests. Estimated size: M (about 400 lines).
data.title: ddflow correct: CLI and MCP surface, permission model, help and README

data.body: Level C of D-record-correction-layers. ddflow scan-records (also a doctor check) searches .ddflow/events, .ddflow/blobs, committed views and exports for the built-in secret shapes plus a layered forbidden-term list read only from the machine-local layer (.ddflow/local/; never committed, never printed in full: findings name file, event id, field and a digest). One pattern set and one term list feed both the scan and write-time redaction (log, view, export profiles) so what the scan flags can no longer be written. Findings are the input of correction and scrub. Everything bounded and configurable ([log].scan_max_files, scan_max_bytes, scan_max_findings, [redact].terms_local). Acceptance: tests that fail before: a planted shape in an event, a blob and a view is found; a local term is found and redacted at write time; a term in the committed config is refused as not local; output never prints the value; the scan is bounded. Estimated size: M (about 450 lines).
data.title: Leak guard: scan-records over events, blobs and views, with a local forbidden-term list, and write-time redaction parity

data.body: D-scrub-person-only. Register the T3 verb scrub.apply (Site row, digest binds the literal digest, the file list and the working-tree state, one use, one hour) and refuse typed-chat approval for it even with accept_chat_for_t3. A test pins that no [approvals].policy rule and no RETRY_VERBS entry names scrub.apply or any T3 verb, and that a standing window or auto_approve_after_retries never answers it. An agent may file the ask and run the dry run, never approve. Acceptance: tests that fail before: policy and retry rules cannot answer scrub.apply; typed chat refused; agent refused with an ask id. Estimated size: S (about 150 lines).
data.title: Scrub approval tier: T3 person-only verb scrub.apply, excluded from every policy rule

data.body: Level B. ddflow scrub --literal-file/--pattern-id (the value never on a command line or in history) lists every file and line it would touch (dry run, default). With --approval it rewrites the working-tree event lines and blobs holding the value with [scrubbed:<id>], keeping event ids, order and line count; a blob that changes is rewritten under its new address and its stub updated in the same pass; appends a scrub.recorded tombstone (event ids touched, digest of each line after the scrub, digest of the pattern, reason, who); the shard-marks and the content-mismatch check treat a line whose digest matches a tombstone as scrubbed (info) and other clones are told scrubbed not lost; writes atomically with a backup outside the repo. It prints the unavoidable follow-ups: rotate the secret first, git history keeps the old text until the operator rewrites and force-pushes (documented git-filter-repo commands, never run), other clones, forks, backups, host caches. It never rewrites history and never pushes. Bounded by scrub_max_files and scrub_max_lines. Acceptance: tests that fail before: dry run touches nothing; apply without approval refused; ids and order preserved and replay folds the same except the scrubbed text; doctor reports scrubbed and not lost/mismatch; a blob is re-addressed consistently; second clone fixture sees scrubbed. Estimated size: L (about 700 lines).
data.title: ddflow scrub: dry-run by default, shard and blob rewrite, tombstone, doctor says scrubbed not lost

data.body: A help topic and runbook with the order: rotate first; correct the record (level A); scrub (level B, person); the exact documented history rewrite commands (git-filter-repo with sensitive-data removal, force push of branches and tags, notify clones and forks, ask the host to purge cached views) marked as the operator's to run; how the lost-events and accept-history states read afterwards. Acceptance: help parity test lists the topic; the text states the limits. Estimated size: S (about 150 lines).
data.title: Runbook: a secret leaked: rotate, correct, scrub, rewrite history

data.body: Forged correction events (wrong kind, unknown field, oversized, non-catalogue field) fail the strict fold; an agent attempting scrub or a policy-window auto-approval is refused; replay after correction and after scrub yields the corrected state; a second clone sees scrubbed not lost; the secret is absent from every derived view, cache, export and brief after both levels. Estimated size: M (about 300 lines).
data.title: Hostile end-to-end tests for correction and scrub

data.text: Operator answers on record correction: (1) an agent may correct its own records and records on an item it holds a lease on without asking, audited; everything else needs the operator. (2) The forbidden-term list is committed in the project config, shared across clones; a layered list, with a hashed or prefix-only form and a clear warning, and a local-only layer still supported and merged; docs say a committed list reveals the terms unless hashed. (3) Scrub backup: ask at each scrub, no default. (4) Scrub approval: person-only T3, no typed-chat relay, never covered by a standing window or policy rule. (5) Resume REC-correct-event now.

data.consequences: Docs and doctor must warn about plain committed terms; scrub has a required flag.
data.decision: Levels A (record.corrected), B (scrub) and C (leak guard) stand as in D-record-correction-layers, with two changes. The forbidden-term list is layered: a committed project-config layer shared by clones plus a local-only layer, merged. The committed layer supports a hashed or prefix-only form; a committed plain list reveals the terms and the tooling warns about it and the docs say so. The scrub command requires an explicit backup choice at every run, with no default.
data.title: Record correction layers: leak-guard term list is layered, committed allowed (hashed form), scrub backup chosen at each scrub

data.decision: An agent may correct a record it authored and records on an item it holds a lease on, without asking, with a required reason and an audit entry. Every other correction needs the operator.
data.title: Who may correct a record: own records and leased-item records, audited; others need the operator
